title: He didn’t wake up weak.
paragraphs:
He didn’t wake up weak.
He woke up empty.

Because you can still look strong…
while God is already gone.
Here’s the part nobody talks about:
Samson didn’t fall when Delilah cut his hair.

He fell…
when he started playing with what God told him to protect.
You don’t lose your calling overnight.
You won’t even feel it at first.

You’ll still lift your hands in worship.
Still post the verses.
Still say “God is good.”
Because this isn’t just Samson’s story.
We flirt with what God told us to flee.
We entertain what God told us to crucify.

We rename disobedience as “struggle”…
and call bondage “just who I am.”
You try to stand like before…
That’s exactly what happened in Book of Judges 16.

“He awoke from his sleep and thought, ‘I will go out as before…’
But he did not know that the Lord had left him.” (Judges 16:20)

Some scholars interpret this not as God abandoning Samson impulsively,
but as the natural consequence of Samson repeatedly breaking his Nazirite vow—
a slow drift away from covenant faithfulness.
Because many today are living in that same illusion.
Let me ask you something that might sting:

What have you been tolerating…
that God already told you to cut off?
But small doors open into big prisons.
Samson thought he could control it.
He thought he could dance on the edge without falling.
He thought his calling was stronger than his compromise.
Samson didn’t just lose his strength.
You justify what used to convict you.
You normalize what used to break you.
This is not where the story ends.

Hidden in the shadows of failure…
was a quiet miracle.
His hair began to grow again.
And maybe that’s where you are right now.
Feeling the weight of what you’ve allowed.
That means your heart is still alive.

Because the worst place to be
is not broken…
Because this is where everything changes.
Samson’s strength didn’t come from his hair.
The hair was just a symbol.
The power was always the presence.
And when Samson finally realized that…
“O Lord God, please remember me and please strengthen me only this once…” (Judges 16:28)
That prayer came from a broken man.
A man who finally saw clearly.
Now here’s where the Gospel breaks in.
Because Samson’s story points to a deeper truth:
You and I don’t just drift.
“For all have sinned and fall short of the glory of God.” (Romans 3:23)
And sin doesn’t just weaken us.
“Your iniquities have made a separation between you and your God.” (Isaiah 59:2)
While we were still in our compromise…
“But God shows his love for us in that while we were still sinners, Christ died for us.” (Romans 5:8)
Every moment we chose darkness over light.
“He himself bore our sins in his body on the tree…” (1 Peter 2:24)
That means your failure doesn’t have the final word.
“Repent therefore, and turn back, that your sins may be blotted out.” (Acts 3:19)
You don’t need to stay empty.
You don’t need to stay bound.
You don’t need to stay blind.
You don’t just get strength back.
“Therefore, if anyone is in Christ, he is a new creation…” (2 Corinthians 5:17)
So let me ask you again—
If this stirred something in you…
